intro: Quick reference for working at the command line and writing small scripts.

sheets.title: Everyday commands
sheets.blurb: Files, text processing, redirection and the editor.

blocks.title: Files and directories
rows: List with details, hidden files, human sizes
cp -a src dst  /  mv a b  /  rm -r dir
Copy (keep attributes), move or rename, remove
Create or update time; show inode details
ln file hard  /  ln -s target link
File type; directory size; free space
Create / extract gzip tar (`-j` bzip2, `-J` xz, `-t` list)

blocks.title: Viewing, searching and editing text
rows: Search recursively, ignore case, line numbers (`-v` invert, `-E` regex, `-c` count)
Pieces; sort; count duplicates; count lines
tr a-z A-Z  /  tee file  /  xargs
Translate; write and pass on; build commands
cmd > file  /  >> file  /  2> err  /  &> all  /  < in
Redirection: overwrite, append, stderr, both, stdin
a | b  /  a && b  /  a || b  /  a ; b
Pipe; run if success; run if failure; sequence
vim: i, Esc, :wq, :q!, /text, dd, yy, p, u
Insert, save and quit, force quit, search, delete line, copy, paste, undo

sheets.title: Permissions and users
sheets.blurb: Permission bits, ownership, users, groups and sudo.

blocks.title: Ownership and special bits
rows: chmod 640 f  /  chmod u+x,g-w,o= f  /  chmod -R
chmod u+s f  /  chmod g+s dir  /  chmod +t dir
setuid (4), setgid (2: new files inherit the group), sticky (1: only the owner can delete)

blocks.title: Users, groups and sudo
rows: Create user with home, shell, supplementary group (`-u`, `-g`, `-d`, `-e`)
Add to a group (without -a you replace the groups)
su - alice  /  sudo -u alice cmd  /  sudo -i
Switch user, run as, root shell
Edit sudo rules safely; example `alice ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl`

blocks.title: Account files
head: File
Holds
rows: name:x:UID:GID:comment:home:shell (UID 0 = root, system accounts below 1000 on most distributions)

blocks.title: Shell scripting
rows: if [ -f file ]; then ...; elif ...; else ...; fi
Test: `-f` file, `-d` dir, `-e` exists, `-z` empty string, `-eq -ne -lt -gt` numbers
for f in *.log; do echo "$f"; done
while read -r line; do ...; done < file
Read a file line by line
Script name, arguments, all arguments, count, last exit status

blocks.title: Containers (Podman / Docker)
rows: Run a container in the background with a port mapping
podman ps -a  /  podman logs web  /  podman exec -it web sh
podman stop web  /  podman rm web  /  podman images  /  podman rmi
Make a systemd unit for the container
Run as a normal user; volumes may need `:Z` to relabel for SELinux
